records.vts_leads: Flamenco Signal Station (Panama Canal Authority): arrival coordination on VHF Ch 12 from 8 nm off the Pacific Sea Buoy; not designated a VTS in N-2-2026
records.vts_boundary_basis: No official source describes a VTS whose area includes Part 1. The Panama Canal Authority's Flamenco Signal Station coordinates Pacific anchorage and harbour movements (N-2-2026) and is called a signal station, not a VTS; N-2-2026 does not name the TSS or define a service area.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (Part I inventory lists only GALREP, VRS-0019, in this region, confined to the Galapagos). COLREG.2/Circ.65, AMP MMC-304 and AMP Circular DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026 attach no reporting requirement to the TSS. The ACP call to Flamenco Signal Station at 8 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy (about 11 nm from Flamenco Island) is canal and anchorage arrival reporting, not a separate MRS. Geographically it falls near the northern (inner) end of the lanes (08°44.7'N to 08°46'N), but the buoy position was not verified from an official source.
records.evidence_summary: IMO B-VIII/1 Part 1, adopted MSC 93 (COLREG.2/Circ.65), in force 1 Dec 2014. Current ACP (A-24-2026) and AMP (DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026) notices refer to the TSS only for the seasonal 10 kn whale recommendation. ACP N-2-2026 requires a VHF Ch 12 call to Flamenco Signal Station 8 nm from the Pacific Sea Buoy. That is canal arrival coordination and does not show a VTS covering the TSS. No Part I MRS. No official source shows VTS coverage, and no official complete list of Panamanian VTS shows that there is none.
records.unresolved_issue: It is not known whether ACP or AMP operates a VTS-designated service whose area includes the Gulf of Panama lanes. ACP says Flamenco is a 'signal station'. Its radar coverage and service area, and the official Pacific Sea Buoy position, remain unconfirmed. There is no official list of Panamanian VTS.
records.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: Unresolved with Flamenco as a lead. The 8 nm arrival call is verified in N-2-2026 and correctly treated as canal arrival reporting, not an MRS

records.reporting_authority: Capitanía de Puerto del Callao (TRAMAR), DICAPI (per NGA Pub. 125)
records.vts_leads: TRAMAR (Callao maritime traffic control office, Capitanía de Puerto del Callao, VHF 16/13, per NGA Pub. 125); 'VTS Callao' (Peruvian Navy, Wärtsilä Navi-Harbour, supplier case study 2025 and Revista de Marina 2023 lead). Probably the same operational entity; do not create two records.
records.vts_boundary_basis: NGA Pub. 125 links the Callao TSS to TRAMAR, the Callao maritime traffic control office. All vessels report at 20, 10 and 4 miles from Isla San Lorenzo and at the Outer Fairway Buoy, which spans the TSS (Parts I to III lie about 2 to 4 nm off Isla San Lorenzo and the port). Pub. 125 does not call TRAMAR a VTS. A Peruvian Navy VTS at Callao (Wärtsilä Navi-Harbour, operating by 2024) is shown only in supplier material. No official source gives its name, area or coverage of the TSS.
records.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (only GALREP, VRS-0019, Galapagos). NGA Pub. 125 (Tier 3, corrected to 27 Aug 2026) makes reports to TRAMAR mandatory for all vessels and ties them explicitly to the TSS. No Peruvian statutory or DICAPI source for the requirement was obtained. The requirement cannot be classed as a formally named national MRS. If TRAMAR is the Callao VTS, it is VTS reporting and not a separate MRS. Recorded as Unresolved, not Yes.
records.evidence_summary: IMO B-VIII/6 (COLREG.2/Circ.48 Annex 4, in force 1 Dec 2000): three parts, a precautionary area and an ATBA off Callao. NGA Pub. 125 says: 'An IMO-adopted Traffic Separation Scheme (TRAMAR) ... All vessels must report to TRAMAR on VHF channel 16' at 20, 10 and 4 miles from Isla San Lorenzo. There is strong evidence that a traffic control or VTS function covers the TSS, but it is Tier 3 (foreign) evidence and does not name a VTS. The DICAPI 2025/2026 Callao anchorage resolutions do not mention TRAMAR or a VTS. The supplier case study and a 2023 naval journal article (404) point to a new 'VTS Callao'. They are lead-only sources. It cannot be classified as VTS until a DICAPI source defines the service and its area.
records.source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.48 1 Jun 2000; Pub. 125 17th ed 2025 corrected to 27 Aug 2026; RD 348-2026 8 Jun 2026; Wärtsilä case study 17 Apr 2025
records.unresolved_issue: Obtain a DICAPI resolution or HIDRONAV radio aids entry establishing 'VTS Callao' / TRAMAR. It should give the official name, service area, VHF channels and participation. Confirm whether it covers all three TSS parts and whether the TRAMAR reports are part of that VTS or a separate national scheme.
records.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: still Unresolved, but a TSS-specific mandatory TRAMAR reporting requirement is now evidenced in Pub. 125. The VTS Callao lead is unchanged and has no official source

batch_audits.pass2_evidence_check: Reopened X-S1 to X-S5, X-S7 and X-S8 locally from the downloaded copies, and X-S13. No positive VTS or MRS association is asserted. Verified that the Flamenco 8 nm call text (N-2-2026 s.2a) does not name the TSS or call Flamenco a VTS. Verified that COLREG.2/Circ.65, MMC-304 and DGPIMA-005-DECCP-2026 contain no reporting or VTS provision. Verified that the Pub. 125 Talara and Paita entries contain no VTS. All sources are current (ACP 2026, AMP 2026, Pub. 125 corrected Aug 2026) except the IMO adoption circulars, which are the in-force instruments.
batch_audits.pass3_classification_duplicate_check: Parent B-VIII/1 is split into three individual TSS. The Flamenco lead applies to Part 1 only. Flamenco is a signal station and is kept as a lead, not a VTS. The canal arrival call is not counted as an MRS. GALREP (VRS-0019) is excluded on geography. Peruvian port radio call signs (Talara Control) are not treated as VTS. No VTS or VRS IDs are needed.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: All five are Unresolved. VTS absence cannot be confirmed without an official Panamanian or Peruvian VTS list. For Panama: whether ACP or AMP operates any VTS covering the Gulf of Panama lanes, and the official Pacific Sea Buoy position.

batch_audits.pass2_evidence_check: Reopened X-S6, X-S7, X-S8 (Sector 3 pp.67, 73, 86, 92, 94), X-S9, X-S10 and X-S14. Callao: the TRAMAR mandatory reporting text is verified verbatim in Pub. 125 (current correction). It names the TSS, but it is Tier 3 and does not describe a VTS, so no positive VTS association is recorded and reporting is held as Unresolved. X-S11 is a supplier page and lead only. X-S12 returned 404 and was not used as evidence. The DICAPI Callao anchorage resolutions (2025, 2026) were checked and do not mention TRAMAR or a VTS.
batch_audits.pass3_classification_duplicate_check: TRAMAR and 'VTS Callao' are probably one entity. They are recorded as a single lead service, not two. The TRAMAR reports may be VTS reporting, so they are not counted as a separate MRS. Pisco (TSS-0184) is the renamed 'Landfall and approaches to Puerto San Martin' (COLREG.2/Circ.48 Annex 5). The coordinator should merge it with any San Martin register entry. Costera Pisco is a coast radio station, not a VTS. No VTS or VRS IDs are needed.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: All five are Unresolved. Callao needs an official DICAPI/HIDRONAV source for the VTS name, area and TSS coverage, and needs to settle whether the TRAMAR reporting is VTS reporting or a national MRS. Salaverry, Chimbote, Pisco and San Nicolás have no official Peruvian VTS list.

method_notes: Research date 29 September 2026. The IMO circulars, ACP/AMP notices, NGA Pub. 125 (17th ed 2025, corrected to 27 Aug 2026) and FAOLEX/El Peruano items were downloaded with curl and text-extracted with pypdf. Passages are quoted from the extracted text. Pub. 125 page locators are PDF page numbers. Access failures: the Revista de Marina 2023 'VTS Callao' article returned HTTP 404 and its Wayback copy was unreachable. The IHO SEPHC Panama national report was blocked by the proxy (legacy.iho.int).
